description:

The Isle of Wight Council meets the criteria against which to direct award under the KCS Procurement Services framework Y20023, which includes continuity of existing goods/services from an awarded supplier, goods/services required are unique/exclusive to one manufacturer/supplier, the supplier is able to supply the required goods/services within the customers timescales and the customer is satisfied that, following their own due diligence, they can identify the supplier that offers best value for their requirement. title: Respite Care Block Booked Beds located on the Isle of Wight for people suffering with Dementia on the Isle of Wight.
description:
The Isle of Wight Council ("the Authority") invites Tenders from suitably qualified suppliers ("Potential Suppliers") for the provision of Respite Care Block Booked Beds on the Isle of Wight for people suffering with Dementia. \r
\r
This procurement follows the Open Procedure under the Public Contract Regulations 2015.\r
\r
The Authority's requirement for respite care can be described as a service which provides a break for an informal carer from their caring role supporting another adult with care and support needs. The service is legally defined as a service.\r
\r
The aim of respite care is to enable personalised, quality, informal care arrangements to be sustained and to maintain a person's independence in their own home for as long as possible. The common factor is not what service is provided, but its purpose: to provide a break which is a positive experience for the person with care needs and the carer\r
\r
This opportunity is divided into two lots. Each lot is a single supplier lot as detailed below: \r
\r
LOT 1 - MODERATE DEMENTIA RESIDENTIAL RESPITE CARE ON THE ISLE OF WIGHT.  \r
This care is for people whose dementia symptoms have become more pronounced who may become more confused and forgetful.  They may get frustrated or angry, and act in unexpected ways, and may need more help with daily activities and self-care. The provision MUST be located on the Isle of Wight.\r
\r
LOT 2 - HIGH DEMENTIA RESIDENTIAL RESPITE CARE ON THE ISLE OF WIGHT.  \r
This care is for people whose dementia symptoms are severe who have started to lose their ability to respond to their environment, to carry on a conversation and, eventually, to control movement.  People at this stage may require around-the-clock assistance with daily personal care. The provision MUST be located on the Isle of Wight.\r
\r
The Authority requires the successful supplier(s) to provide one (1) bed with respite care for eligible Service Users for each lot.   \r
\r
The respite care bed (in each lot) must be located on the Isle of Wight and must be available seven days per week and should be bookable up to 12 months in advance for periods from one weekend to two weeks. \r
\r
The respite care bed will be paid for by the Authority irrespective of utilisation, subject to the Schedule 3 No 6 of the Terms and Conditions relating to the bed being empty for more than 7 days, ensuring that the respite care bed is always available to the Authority to utilise for its Service Users' respite care needs.\r
\r
The total allocated annual budget will be reviewed annually in line with the Authority's fee review process.\r
\r
The term of the contract shall be 24th February 2025 to 23rd February 2029 with the option to extend for up to a further 24 months at the sole discretion of the Authority. \r
\r
The closing date for receipt of Tenders is 14:00 Hrs on 10th December 2024.\r
\r

title: Electronic Care Solution for the Isle of Wight Council's Internal Care Homes - short term reablement care homes, community outreach (domiciliary) and long term learning disability care homes.
description:
The Isle of Wight Council (The Authority) invited Tenders from Potential Suppliers for the provision of an Electronic Care Solution for the Isle of Wight Council's internal care homes- short term reablement care homes, community outreach (domiciliary) and long term learning disability care homes. To be awarded to a sole supplier under the Digital Social Care Records Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) Framework Agreement via Department of Health and Social Care.
The Authority requires the provision of a digital system covering four different areas of digitalisation including a care planning tool /system for short-term respite and reablement care home services and long-term learning disability care homes service. The system needs to have a person's pen picture, care and support needs, any risk assessments and tools for staff to complete on a daily basis, for example, diary notes, fluid charts, care interventions. Digital Reception that acts as a visitors' book for people coming into the care home services including staff and giving all visitors the chance to comment on their visit by a quality assurance survey that they complete on their exit. The system will all support the 'roll call' in the event of a fire. Electronic Medication recording (e-MAR) that is linked to the care planning tool that will list a persons medications and will give the team the chance to record what medication is given and the actual time it is administered and finally, an electronic rostering system for the domiciliary care service that will schedule the visits staff will do for people in their own homes along with displaying an simple pen picture of the person being visited and any risks that visiting staff will need to be aware of. The system will also provide a safeguard to staff for lone working as well as have the ability to produce reports to demonstrate the performance of the service. The full specification can be seen at Appendix A within the tender documents. 

The initial term duration will be three years with the with the option to extend for up to a further 24 months in 12 month sections at the sole discretion of the Authority.

title: The Isle of Wight Specialist Sexual and Reproductive Health Service
description:
The Isle of Wight Council ("the Authority") are seeking to deliver a Sexual and Reproductive Health Service on the Isle of Wight.  

The Authority requires a service for 12 months as the current contract will be ending in 2023 and the Authority will join other local commissioners in tendering an integrated level 3 Sexual Health Service across Isle of Wight, Hampshire, Portsmouth and Southampton to start in April 2024.

The aim of the service is to improve sexual health through the delivery of a range of accessible, high-quality, responsive, cost-effective, confidential, Integrated Sexual Health Services through a branded hub and spoke model of service provision to the local population. The service will also support the delivery of level 1 and 2 sexual health services in primary care and other community settings through clinical and system leadership and the development and provision of professional training, care pathways and the co-ordination of a local sexual health network. 

Level 3 clinical services shall be Consultant-led and provided via a One-Stop Hub and Spoke Model. This service model includes the provision of the following Level 3 Sexual & Reproductive Health Services. 

Access to the service should be through a range of appointment types, such as face to face, virtual, telephone and online.  The Provider is required to ensure effective working relationships with commissioners and staff of interdependent services including existing HIV and termination of pregnancy services and with commissioners of national vaccination programmes for people at increased risk of certain infections to enable delivery of seamless pathways for service users.

title: Provision of Ventnor Harbour Management
description:
The Authority invites Tenders from suitably qualified suppliers to undertake the provision of the management of Ventnor Harbour, Isle of Wight.

The Potential Supplier will be expected to manage all aspects of the harbour at Ventnor; typically, this will include but is not limited to: -

•	Supervision of the harbour
•	Management of the berths
•	Collection of berthing income
•	Maintenance of the pontoons and harbour infrastructure
•	Full insuring liability
•	Reporting all accidents and incidents
•	Provision of monthly, quarterly and annual reports
•	Compliance with the Port Marine Safety Code (PMSC)
•	Compliance with all relevant legislation, including Health and Safety
•	Statutory returns to the Marine Management Organisation (MMO)
•	Removal of seaweed in accordance with the current MMO licence

The Potential Supplier will benefit from the total income derived from mooring fees, and, subject to the Authority's prior approval and all relevant permissions, may be able to implement improvements which may also generate additional income during the term of the contract. 

There will be costs associated with managing Ventnor Harbour, not least the annual requirement of seaweed removal, which currently cost in the region of £103,000 per annum, though this can be reviewed as necessary by the successful supplier. All operating costs will be the responsibility of the Potential Supplier, a summary of the last 3 years income and expenditure can be found in Appendix 2 of the Tender Pack. 

The term of the contract shall be 01st April 2023 until 31st March 2028. The Authority's long-term intention is to dispose of the freehold of the harbour to a third party, however, in order to be able to do this it will be necessary to either obtain a Harbour Revision Order or have its statutory port designation removed.  a) Support service users holistic wellbeing through enabling behaviour change and supporting engagement with other services.\r
 b) Support service users to access appropriate services, acting as an advocate for those who have problems around access and inclusion.\r
c ) Support service users to access community resources and personal development opportunities.\r
d)  Support service users to make the best use of local resources and amenities to meet their health and welfare needs.\r

title: The Bay Area Place Plan
description:
The Bay Area Place plan will be action-based research, which seeks to influence policy and delivery. This study should aim to be a catalyst for change in internal community perceptions as well as external perceptions, and there should be a focus on involving many of those who would be of critical importance on implementing any transition approach advocated in the study report.

The Study should use official data, such as the IMD and the Census data, to build up a statistical profile of the LSOAs that make up The Bay Area. It should also use CACI Paycheck data to develop a detailed understanding of current household income levels across each of the LSOAs. It will be critical, however, to go beyond this quantitative data to establish a complete understanding of the 'lived experience' of different communities in the area. Upon establishing a thorough understanding of the linkages between the socio-economic and cultural components of different communities in the area, the study should seek to focus on holistic solutions.

The term of the contract shall be February 2023 until April/May 2023 with the option to extend for up to a further 3 months at the sole discretion of the Authority.

      Restorative Justice brings those harmed by crime and those responsible for the harm into communication with each other. Restorative Justice offers victims an opportunity to be heard, to ask questions of the offender and to have their say in what they want to happen next. For some people who have been affected by crime, it can help them to explore why the crime happened. It can also help victims to move forward and feel less fearful of crime in the future. Evidence shows that people who take part in a Restorative Justice Process come away feeling satisfied because it has allowed them to have their say. title: HIWFRS FIRE COVER REVIEW AND OPTIMISATION MODELLING
description:
Hampshire and Isle of Wight Fire and Rescue Service (HIWFRS) has contracted Operational Research in Health Ltd (ORH) to undertake a Fire Cover Review to support the planning of resourcing across Hampshire and the Isle of Wight. 

The key objectives of this project are to review response standards and create and setup appropriate models of fire cover. Optimisation modelling will be used to assess configurations using existing and greenfield locations. Appliance contribution and efficiency saving modelling will be completed which will feed into the modelling around bespoke configurations. 

Specialist appliances RTC risk will also be assessed. The 
proposed scope is provided below in this document with costs and anticipated timescales associated with each work item. 

During the project, ORH will provide HIWFRS with regular updates through a combination of in-person and virtual meetings. At key milestones (risk analysis, model setup, initial modelling, etc) ORH will produce presentations of progress to date, which will be shared with HIWFRS. 

On completion of the project, ORH will provide a summary report of the methodology and key findings supported by an in-depth document that 
includes results for all modelling options. 

ORH anticipates that this project will take 16 weeks to complete, from receipt of all necessary data and a purchase order number from HIWFRS.

title: Solihull online parenting multi-user licence  and professional training package.
description:
Five-year registration opportunity and then lifetime access, for those registered users, to the Solihull Approach online courses to support parental education and strategies from Conception to 19 years to increase understanding of child development stages and behaviours. Unlimited professional access to 3 online training courses, due to individual access, for 12 months within the five-year contract.
Target Group:
• Families living in Hampshire and the Isle of Wight
• Professionals involved in working with children, young people and families in Hampshire and the Isle of Wight from the following services: Public health, Nursing, Children's Services, Midwifery, Primary care, Education, Libraries and voluntary organisations.

The Solihull online parenting courses and professional training package are within the Investing in Public Health projects funded by the Public Health ring fenced grant. This project is designed to fill the identified gap for families through the provision of a digital resource which covers the childhood years, to improve the knowledge, skills 
and confidence of families to meet the needs of children and young people at any stage of child development. This is a necessity and will improve interactions between parents/Carers and children and reduce inequalities through early intervention.
